So many people don't understand what insurance is for. It's never a good economic proposition to buy insurance for costs you could easily bear without it.
It might be a good economic proposition, if you get a group discount, or a subsidy.

I probably shouldn't have said "never", but in aggregate, it basically is. If an insurer is to remain solvent it needs to take in more money than it pays out. If every policyholder makes a claim of $100 on an insurance policy, the insurance company will need to collect an additional $100 from every policyholder to break even - with overhead it is of course more than $100, so everyone would have been better just paying the $100 out of pocket directly.

The way it ends up working out is that if insurance covers cheap routine things like physicals and birth control pills, it essentially becomes a pre-pay plan rather than insurance. I had a catastrophic insurance plan (10K deductible) for something like $60/month, and when Obamacare was enacted, the new minimum plan was a LOT more than $255/year more expensive than my old one. Sure, I could get free physicals now, but I'd have to get one every week to make up for the increased cost.
